verdict.rationale: Aider ships a few fixed, built-in event triggers. Watch mode acts on file saves containing AI!/AI? comments, `--auto-test` with a user-supplied `--test-cmd` runs after every AI edit, and it lints and commits automatically after edits. There is no general facility for defining arbitrary event→action rules. Missing for 10: user-definable rules over arbitrary events, configurable trigger conditions beyond the built-in edit/save hooks, a choice of custom actions beyond test/lint commands, and independent corroboration of automation depth.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: You can configure aider to run your test suite after each time the AI edits your code using the --test-cmd <test-command> and --auto-test switch.
If you run aider with `--watch-files`, it will watch all files in your repo and look for any AI coding instructions you add using your favorite IDE or text editor.
AI! triggers aider to make changes to your code.
By default, aider will lint any files which it edits.
